decisions.reason: As a prominently launched next-generation core machine, it likely meets or stays close enough to aspiration levels for a large German machinery firm to retain it while exploiting sunk development and sales complementarities.
This software add-on is somewhat niche, but as part of the firm's broader inline-printing portfolio it is inexpensive to carry and likely kept unless performance clearly falls short of aspirations.

An inkjet coder for non-absorbent surfaces fits the firm's core coding equipment business, so boundedly rational management would usually continue it absent strong evidence of persistent underperformance.

The decoding app is more peripheral than the machinery products, but as a successor to an earlier app and a complement to installed products it would more likely be retained than withdrawn immediately.
An inline code verification system is strategically complementary to marking equipment and quality assurance needs, making continuation likely unless its results are well below aspiration levels.
Because the print layout design software was given homepage visibility and supports the core installed base, the firm likely sees enough strategic value and slack to keep it on the market.
